architecture: The service consists of a thin Express HTTP layer (app) that wires middleware (rate limiting, JSON body parsing, trust‑proxy handling) and routes (router). The router implements three endpoints: POST /shorten, GET /:code, GET /healthz. Business logic is delegated to helper modules: `codeGenerator` creates random 7‑character base62 strings with collision retry; `db` wraps a single SQLite file (better‑sqlite3) with a schema `links(code TEXT PRIMARY KEY, url TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)` and runs in WAL mode. `rateLimiter` configures `express-rate-limit` to enforce 60 requests per minute per client IP, returning 429 with `Retry‑After`. Configuration values (PORT, DB_PATH, BASE_URL, TRUST_PROXY) are read once by the `config` module and exported as a plain object. The `server` module is the entry point that calls `app.listen` using the configured port. All components are pure Node.js with only the declared dependencies (express, express-rate-limit, better-sqlite3). Docker builds a minimal Node LTS Alpine image, installs only production dependencies, creates a non‑root user, declares `VOLUME /data`, exposes port 3000, and runs `node src/server.js`. No telemetry, no external calls, and the MIT license is applied throughout. The README documents environment variables, Docker usage, and example curl commands. The test suite uses the built‑in `node:test` runner with `supertest` against an in‑memory SQLite DB to verify shortening, redirection, validation, rate limiting, and error handling.

modules.name: config
modules.purpose: Read environment variables, provide defaults, and export a typed configuration object used by all other modules.
modules.contract: Exports a constant `config` with properties: `port` (number, default 3000), `dbPath` (string, default '/data/shortener.db'), `baseUrl` (string | undefined), `trustProxy` (boolean|string|number|array, default false). No side effects. Owned file: src/config.js. Tested by unit test that sets process.env and verifies exported values.

modules.name: db
modules.purpose: Initialize the SQLite database, ensure schema exists, and provide CRUD functions for short links.
modules.contract: Exports functions: `init()` (creates DB connection, sets WAL mode, creates `links` table if missing), `insertLink(code:string, url:string, createdAt:number): void`, `findUrlByCode(code:string): string|undefined`. Throws on DB errors. Owned file: src/db.js. Tested with an in‑memory SQLite DB by calling `init` then CRUD functions.

modules.name: codeGenerator
modules.purpose: Generate a unique 7‑character base62 code, retrying up to 5 times on collision.
modules.contract: Exports async function `generateUniqueCode(): Promise<string>` that returns a 7‑char string. Internally uses `crypto.randomInt` to build a base62 string, checks uniqueness via `db.findUrlByCode`, retries up to 5 times, and throws if all attempts fail. Owned file: src/codeGenerator.js. Tested by mocking `db.findUrlByCode` to simulate collisions and success.

modules.name: rateLimiter
modules.purpose: Configure and export an Express middleware that limits each client IP to 60 requests per minute.
modules.contract: Exports a middleware `rateLimiter` created with `express-rate-limit` using a window of 60 seconds, max 60, standard rate‑limit headers, and a JSON 429 response with `Retry-After`. Owned file: src/rateLimiter.js. Tested by sending >60 requests with supertest and asserting 429 and header.

modules.name: router
modules.purpose: Define the three public routes and their handlers, delegating to db and codeGenerator.
modules.contract:
Exports an Express `Router` instance with routes:
- POST /shorten: validates JSON body `{url}`, checks scheme and length, generates a code via `codeGenerator.generateUniqueCode`, stores it with `db.insertLink`, and returns 201 JSON `{code, shortUrl, url}`.
- GET /:code: validates `code` matches /^[0-9A-Za-z]{7}$/, looks up URL via `db.findUrlByCode`, redirects 302 or returns 404 JSON.
- GET /healthz: returns 200 JSON `{status:"ok"}`.
All routes use `rateLimiter` middleware. Owned file: src/router.js. Tested with supertest covering success, validation errors, unknown code, and rate limit.

modules.name: app
modules.purpose: Create the Express application, apply global middleware, and mount the router.
modules.contract:
Exports a function `createApp(): Express` that:
- Instantiates Express.
- Calls `app.set('trust proxy', config.trustProxy)`.
- Uses `express.json()` for body parsing.
- Applies `rateLimiter` globally.
- Mounts `router` at `/`.
- Returns the configured app instance. Owned file: src/app.js. Tested by creating the app and asserting middleware presence and route registration.

modules.name: server
modules.purpose: Entry point that starts the HTTP server on the configured port.
modules.contract: When executed, imports `createApp` from `app`, calls it, and invokes `app.listen(config.port, () => console.log(...))`. No exported symbols. Owned file: src/server.js. Tested by spawning the server on an ephemeral port and performing a health check.

modules.name: infra
modules.purpose: Provide a reproducible Docker image that runs the service as a non‑root user, exposes port 3000, and declares a data volume.
modules.contract: Dockerfile uses node:lts-alpine, copies package*.json and src/, runs `npm ci --omit=dev`, creates user `node` (uid 1000), sets `WORKDIR /app`, `VOLUME /data`, `EXPOSE 3000`, and `CMD ["node","src/server.js"]`. Includes a `.dockerignore` that excludes node_modules, test files, and git metadata. Also provides `docker-compose.yml` mounting a named volume to `/data`. Owned files: Dockerfile, .dockerignore, docker-compose.yml. Tested by building the image (`docker build .`) and running a container that responds to `/healthz`.
